text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Five schoolgirls assassinated in Berrouaghia, south of Algiers.
- The foreign ministry denies a report that the United Nations has rejected Algeria's invitation to send observers to supervise the June 5 parliamentary elections.
- A bomb explosion kills the brother and a cousin of a "terrorist" member of the Islamic Salvation Army.
- French police arrest members of the Algerian Islamist Hamas party in France.
- Privatisation of state-owned enterprises will be speeded up in the second half of 1997 and in 1998.
- Twelve food processing enterprises have been slated for privatisation.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia heads the Algerian delegation to Lome meeting over Zaire crisis.
- Algeria has contacted 100 United Nations members inviting them to dispatch observers to supervise legislative elections to be held on June 5.
